AKM Shafiqur Rahman with Mustafa Niaz Muhammad, Shahabuddin Foez and Mustafa Kamal Pasha ----- For the Petitioners. 
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury  ----- For the State.
parties:
Md Ansarul Alam & others ----- Petitioners
vs
State & another ----- Opposite-Party
full_judgment:
FHM Habibur Rahman J : This Rule under section 439 CrPC was issued on 8-12-85 at the instance of the ten accused-petitioners calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong and informant Opposite party No. 2 Mohammad Mozammel Haque asking them to show cause why Order No. 94 date 10-11-85 Passed by the Session Judge, Chittagong in ST Case No. 13 of 1980 refusing to release the accused petitioners under section 8 on. Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 should not be set-aside or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The case for the prosecution is that both the parties live in village Karan Khain, Police Station Patiya, District Chittagong. There was a quarrel between informant Mozammel Haque and his supporters and the accused party men on the night of 17-3-79 at 9-00 PM over the marriage of one Shajahan on 18-3-79 at about 7-00 AM accused Haji Hafez Ahmed Sowdagar (since, dead), Md. Ansarul Alam (son of accused Hafiz), Joynal Abedin, Nasiruddin, Abul Bashar, Abdul Quddus, Bazal Ahmed (brother of accused Hafez Ahmed), Nazrul Islam, Emdadul Islam (sons of accused Bazal Ahmed), Abu Taher, Ekhlash, Abu Taleb and Feroz Mia (brother of accused Joynal Abedin) being armed with deadly weapons including gun came to the house of the informant party in furtherance of their common intention to murder informant's brother Illias, informant Mozammel, Nurul Alam and Alek Khan and attacked them. Accused Bazu Ahmed, Nazrul Islam, Emdadul Islam, Feroz Mia, etc, encouraged Hafez Ahmed to shoot from his gun which accused Ansarul Alam had brought from his house and handed over to his father accused Hafez Ahmed and on the order given by accused Joynal Abedin, accused Hafez Ahmed fired upon Illias, Nurul Alam and Alek Khan Illias was fatally wounded by gun shot. He became unconscious, Nurul Alam and Alek Khan were also wounded by gun shot Illias was removed in an unconscious state to his house. But soon after he was brought to his house he succumbed to the gunshot injury. All the 13 accused-persons bad started variously assaulting informant. Mohammed Mozammel Haque and Illias before the firing by accused Hafez Ahmed. Accused Nasiruddin injured witness Md Ali with a spade. Accused Abul Bashar injured witness Md. Ali with a kirich, Accused Ansarul Alam gave a blow by kirich on the head of witness Md Ali. All the 13 accused variously assaulted the witnesses. Informant Mohammed Mozammel Haque lodged FIR with PS Patiya on 18-3-79 at 12-30 hours. The Police investigated into the case and submitted charge-sheet on 14-7-79 under sections 147, 148, 447, 324, 326, 302-34 of the Penal Code against accused Hafez Ahmed, Md. Ansarul Alam, Joynal Abedin, Nasiruddin, Abul Bashar, Abdul Quddus, Bazal Ahrtied, Nazrul Islam, Emdadul Islam, Abu Taher, Ekhlash, Abu Taleb and Feroz Mia all of whom were allowed bail. The Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Sadar (North) Chittagong sent the case to the. Sessions Judge, Chittagong by his order dated 18-9-79. On 3-1-80 the Sessions Judge, Chittagong passed the following order: 

 "Record received froth SDO (s) at Patiya, Chittagong as per Law Reforms Ordinance Of 1978. Registered. Let this case be transferred to the learned Second' Court of the Additional Sessions Judge, Chittagong for favour of disposal." 

 3. Thus before any of the accused persons had appeared before the Sessions Judge, Chittagong, be transferred the case for disposal to the Second Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Chittagong on 3-1-80 after taking cognizance. On that very day on behalf of the prosecution a petition for cancellation for the bail of the accused persons was filed. The Sessions Judge transferred that petition also to the Second Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Chittagong for disposal. Out of the 13 accused persons except accused Nazrul Islam other 12 accused persons appeared on 17-1-80 and were allowed to continue on the previous bail. Then the Additional Sessions Judge started trying to secure the attendance of absconding accused Nazrul Islam. On 5-6-80 accused Feroz Mia remained absent. It appears that on 17-6-80 accused Feroz Mia and Hafez Ahmed absconded. Accused Nazrul Islam continued to abscond. Order No. 24 dated 2-5-81 shows that the death certificate was filed by the son of accused Hafez Ahmed showing the accused Hafez Ahmed had died on 15-3-81. Although accused Nazrul Islam surrendered ultimately, but accused Abul Bashar and accused Emdadul Islam remained absconding till date. It also appears from the order dated 2-7-82 that accused Bazal Ahmed with the permission of the Court went away to perform Hajj when the Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 came into force on 21-8-82. It appears from the order dated 3-2-83 that the learned Additional Sessions Judge passed an order that absconding accused Abul Bashar will be tried in his absence under section 339B(2) CrPC. It appears from the order dated 17-8-82 that accused Emdadul Islam was allowed to be represented by his lawyer agent till the stage of section 265 CrPC. It also appears from the said order dated 17-7-83 that accused Abu Taleb also remained absent on that date. On 30-11-83 bail of accused Emdadul Islam was cancelled and his permission to appear through lawyer agent was rescinded. On 21-4-84 it was noted that accused Emdadul Islam was being tried on his absence under section 339(2) CrPC. Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 came into force on 8-8-83; but before that date on 17-7-83 the learned Additional Sessions Judge stayed further proceedings of the case on the ground that the Public Prosecutor had filed the prayer for stay on the following ground : 

 1. That it appears from Memo No. A-2241/ML/ PC/PL dated 19-6-83 from ZMLA Zone "C" (Press & Legal Branch), Chittagong Cantonment that the authority has decided to transfer the case to the Martial Law Court. 

 2. That under the circumstances it is necessary to stay hearing of the case in this Court." 

 4. Although this order of stay was vacated formally on 28-8-84 by the learned Additional Sessions Judge on receipt of Memo No. 3128 dated 28-8-84 from the Sessions Judge, Chittagong, but it appears from the order dated 12-7-84 that it was decided that accused Abul Bashar and accused Emdadul Islam shall be tried in their absence under section 339B(2) CrPC. and on that date charges under sections 302/34; 326/34 and 148 of the Penal Code were framed against all the 12 accused persons including absconding accused Abul Bashar and Emdadul Islam. It appears from the order dated 29-9-84 that PW 1 Md Ali was examined by the prosecution and cross-examined by the defence on the ground that the said witness was going abroad. As the Additional Sessions Judge was busy with other cases, the present case could not be taken for trial although witnesses remained present on various dates. Thereafter, it appears from the order dated 9-9-85 that the Sessions Judge withdrew the present case to his own file for trial. All the 10 accused petitioners filed an application on 9-11-85 through their Advocate stating that by virtue, of the provision of section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 which came into force on 8-8-83. They had acquired the right to be released on 13th September, 1985 by stopping further proceedings of trial and consequently they should be released forthwith. The learned Sessions Judge rejected the petition holding, inter alia, as follows: 

 "In this case charge-sheet under sections 302/34 and under some other sections was submitted on 14-7-79 and the Court of Sessions received the record on 31,80 and cognizance was taken on that date and the case was transferred to the 2nd Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Chittagong for disposal. This indicates that the cognizance of the case was taken long before the promulgation of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982. The provisions of section 339C of CrPC are not applicable in the present case, but the present case is governed by section 35(c) of the said Ordinance (No  XXIV of 1982).................. 

 The provision of section 35(C) of Ordinance XXIV of 1982 is merely directory and an accused is not entitled to be released on the expiry of the period of limitation. The learned Advocate for the accused submitted that this provision of section 35 of Ordinance XXIV of 1982 has been given a go-by by the provisions of Ordinance XXXVII of 1983 (Gazetted on 8-8-83) wherein it has been provided that trial of all pending cases should be concluded within 30-9-85 (failing which further proceeding in respect of the trial shall stand stopped and the accused persons released)  have already found that the time limit has been prescribed under two sections, namely section 339C of CrPC and section 35 of Ordinance XXIV of 1982 By (section 8 of) Ordinance XXXVII of 1983 a directive has been given to conclude trial of all cases pending (on the commencing day of the said Ordinance) on 8th August, 1983 before the aforesaid Court by 31-12-83 which was subsequently extended (by various amending Ordinances) upto 30-9-85 irrespective of time limit prescribed under section 339C of CrPC. Section 8 of Ordinance XXXVII of 1983 is very much silent on the provisions of section 35 of Ordinance XXIV of 1982 which also prescribed a(directory) time limit of 360 days for conclusion of trial of those cases which were pending on the promulgation of Ordinance XXIV of 1982. Ordinance XXXVII of 1983 therefore, has not in any way affected or amended or superseded the provisions of section 35 of Ordinance XXIV of 1982. The intention of the legislature is very much clear by the provisions of section 8 of Ordinance XXXVII of 1983. They have clearly excluded from the consideration the provision of section 35 of Ordinance XXIV of 1982. In that view of the matter, I hold that the present case is not hit by provisions of (section 8) of Ordinance XXXVII of 1983 and the accused persons cannot be released on the ground that the trial could not be concluded within 30-9-85. 

 Furthermore, from the perusal of the record it is found that the learned Additional Sessions Judge, and Court by his order dated 17-7-83 stayed all further proceedings of the case on the ground that the same was under process for being transferred to the Martial Law Court and the learned Additional Sessions Judge directed for noting the same in the register. From the perusal of the record it is found that by order dated 28-8-84 the stay order earlier issued on 17-7-83 was vacated. This indicates that the proceedings of the case was stayed from 17-7-83 to 28-8-84.   This indicates that the case was not pending for disposal on the date of the promulgation of Ordinance XXXVII of 1983. As the further proceeding of the case was stayed by the order of the Court it cannot be construed that the trial of the case was pending on that date. In that view of matter also I hold that Ordinance XXXVII of 1983 is not, applicable in the present case................. 

 Mr AKM Shafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the accused petitioners submits that in view of the provisions of section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 read with Ordinance No. XXIX of 4985, in the facts and circumstances of the present case cognizance of which was taken on 3-1-80 by the learned Sessions Judge, the accused petitioners acquired the right to be released on 30 September, 1985 and that the trial by operation of law stood stopped on the aid dote 30 September 1985. He submits that the learned Sessions Judge committed an error of law by not releasing the accused persons stopping the trial, that the order of the learned Sessions Judge is liable to be set-aside and that the accused should be released on stopping the trial of the Sessions case in question. 

 6. For clear understanding of section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 it is necessary to notice the fact that by Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 (read with Ordinance No. LX of 1982) section 339C was newly inserted for the first time in the Code of Criminal Procedure providing time limit for concluding trial of a case and also providing what if the trial cannot be concluded within the specified time or extended time, further proceedings in respect of the trial shall stand stopped and the accused person released. The law makers were aware about pendency of a very large number of cases in which cognizance had already been taken before the coming into force of Ordinance No.XXIV of 1982 on 21-8-82 and so far those pending cases it was specially provided in section 35(C) of Ordinance XXIV of 1982 as follow: 

 "35. Transitory Provisions Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any amendment made in the said Code by this Ordinance-... (e) any case, including an appeal, other than a case or appeal in respect of an offence under section 400 or section 401 of the Penal Code (Act XLV of 1860), which immediately before the commencement of this Ordinance, was pending in any Court, including the Supreme Court shall be disposed of within a period of three hundred and sixty days from the date of such commencement." 

 7. It is well settled that a case becomes a pending case as soon as cognizance of the offence is taken by a competent Court. In the instant case after the submission of charge-sheet on 14-7-79 and transmission of the case record from the Court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate to the Court of the learned Sessions Judge took cognizance of the offence no 3-1-80. Therefore, since 3-1-80, this A as a pending case and as such the present case comes within the purview of section 35(c) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 and does not come within the mischief of the newly inserted section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure which come into force on 21-8-82 by Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982, section 35(C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 provides that any case which was pending in any Court (on 21-8-82) shall be disposed of within a period of 360 days from the date of commencement of the Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982, that is, from 21-8-82: but section 35(C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 does not significantly provide that on the failure of dispose of the case within the said period the trial shall stand stopped and the accused person shall stand released. Thus section 35(C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 is directory and not mandatory. It is well settled that changes in the procedural law or adjective law made in the stature have retrospective effect unless contrary intention is expressed in the stature or unless there be some good reason against taking such view. In the Book on Interpretation of Statutes by Maxwell, 9th Edition, Page 233 it has been observed: "The general principle, however, seems to be that alterations in procedure are retrospective, unless there be some reason against it. "This view follows from the decisions in the cases of James Gardner vs Edward A Lucas, (1878) 3 AC 582; Colonial Sugar Refining Co. vs Irving, 1905 AC 169 and Delhi Cloth and General Mills Co. Ltd. vs Income Tax Commissioner, Delhi, AIR 1927 PC 242. In the last mentioned case it has been observed by the Privy Council that provisions of a statute dealing merely with matters of procedure may have retrospective effect attributed to them unless that consecration be textually inadmissible. In the present case the law makers by providing special provision for pending case in section 35(C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 have made it abundantly clear that provisions of newly inserted section 339C CrPC shall not apply to cases which were pending on 21-9-82, that is the cases in which cognizance had already been taken by the competent court before 21-8-82 which is the date of commencement of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982. 

 "(8). Special extension of time limit in certain case.-Notwithstanding the time specified in section 339C of the said Code, trial of any case pending, on the commencement of this Ordinance, before a Magistrate or a Sessions Judge, Additional Sessions Judge or Assistant Sessions Judge shall continue and be concluded before the 30th September, 1985; and if such trial cannot be concluded before that date, further proceedings in respect of the trial shall stand stopped and the accused person released." 

 9. In the present case while narrating the facts of the case we have already shown that the learned Sessions Judge received the case on 3-1-80 from the Sub-Divisional Magistrate and consequently took cognizance of the offence on that date, but without securing the attendance of any of the accused petitioners he transferred the case to the Second Court of the Additional Sessions fudge, Chittagong. We have also shown that when Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 came into force on 8-8-83 the trial of the present case could not commence and charge could not be framed, So it cannot be said that when Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 came into force on 8-8-83 the trial of the present case was pending although it is true that since the cognizance as been taken on 3-1-80 the case was pending, The expression used in section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 is "trial of any case pending on the commencement of this Ordinance". There is a significant and substantial difference between the expression "a pending case" and "the trial of a case pending" (as used in said section 8 of Ordinance No, XXXVII of 1983), For a clear understanding of the matter as to when a trial can be said to commence it is useful to quote the following provisions of section 35(a) of Ordinance No, XXIV of 1982, 

 "35, Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any amendment made in the said Code by this Ordinance—(a) any case (other than an appeal) which, immediately before the commencement of this Ordinance, was pending in a Court of Sessions and is triable by a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class under the provisions of the said Code as amended by this Ordinance shall— 

 (i) if trial of such case has already commenced, be disposed of by that court as if no such amendment had been made; 

 (i) if trial of such case has not already commenced, on such commencement, stand transferred for disposal to the Metropolitan Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class, as the case may be, having jurisdiction to try the case." 

 10. Although the tern, "trial" has nowhere been defined in the Code of Criminal Procedure, yet we get the clue from section 35(a) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 itself that a trial cannot be said to commence unless of accusation is stated to the accused or a charge is framed against the accused and it is well settled that a trial ends when the accused is acquitted or convicted. A case becomes a pending case as soon as cognizance is taken by a competent Court. But the trial of a case cannot be said to be pending unless the trial has commenced and the trial cannot commence unless a charge is framed or substance of accusation is stated to the accused. In the present case on the commencement of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 on 8-8-83 the learned. Sessions Judge could not even consider the record of the case under section 265 CrPC. Thus when the Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 came into force, on 8-8-83, due to efforts being made by the trial court to secure the appearance of the absconding accused persons and due to the stay order, charge could not be framed and trial could not commence and therefore, it cannot be said that the trial of the case was pending when Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 came into force on 8-8-83. Consequently, section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 has no manner of application in the present case. 

 11. Further in section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 instead of using the expression "Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force" or instead of using the expression "Notwithstanding the time specified in section 339C of the Code and section 35 (C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982" the law makers deliberately used the expression "Notwithstanding the time specified under section 339C of the Code "and significantly omitted to include in the non-obstinate clause the time specified in section 35(C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982. Provisions of section 339C CPC regarding stopping of trial and release of the accused persons apply only to cases cognizance of which was taken on or after 21-8-82 the date of coming into force of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982. It is well settled that there is no provision for stopping of trial and release of accused in respect of cases covered by section 35(C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 which is directory and not mandatory. The expressions, "Notwithstanding the time specified in section 339C of the said Code ", "trial of any case pending on the commencement of this Ordinance "shall continue" and the marginal note "Special extension of time limit in certain cases" used in section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 clearly indicate that in spite of contrary provisions regarding time limit in section 339C CrPC. the trial of cases pending on b-8-83 coming within the mischief of section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure are to be concluded before 30 September 1985 failing which the trial shall stand stopped and the accused shall stand released and section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 does not include cases covered by section 35 (C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982. In Halsbury's Laws of England, 3rd Edition, Vol 36, page 402 it has been stated as follows; 

 12. In the case of Bangladesh vs Abdul Mannan, 29 DLR (SC) 17 it was observed: 

 In the present case in the non-obstante clause in section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 the newly inserted section 339C CrPC has been expressly mentioned by using the expression "Notwithstanding the time specified in section 339C of the said Code" and section 35 (C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 has been deliberately excluded, thereby making section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 only applicable to cases coming within the mischief of section 339C CrPC. on 8-8-83 excluding the pending cases covered by section 35 (C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982.
